analysis.title: Oracle Default Risk Hits 20%, CCC Spreads Break 1,000bps
key_insights: Oracle 5-year CDS trades near a record 261bps, implying roughly a 20% probability of default over five years, assuming a 40% recovery rate (Bloomberg).
US CCC-rated credit spreads have breached 1,000bps, and the ratio of CCC spreads to overall high-yield spreads is at a record high, so credit is punishing its weakest borrowers (MS).
S&P 500 market breadth is at levels rarely seen in four decades, with only the dot-com bubble period worse (GIR). Headline index performance is diverging from the broader market.
Financials had their largest weekly outflow since March 2026 (BofA).
US banks are the most oversold relative to the S&P 500 since 1993, per Morgan Stanley.
Money market funds took in their biggest inflow since April 2020 (EPFR).

Hedge fund long/short ratio is in the 0th percentile on a 1-year look-back, and fundamental long/short net exposure is in the 2nd percentile of its five-year history (GS Prime). The rally has hurt underexposed hedge funds.
Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at -1.3 standard deviations, showing positioning at the bearish end of its historical range.

The Market Ear's bottom line is that credit is nervous, breadth is deteriorating and banks are under pressure, but with hedge funds already at historic extremes the question is whether anyone is left to sell.
